judgmentFindings.title: Certified submission has no client submission ID; a retry creates a second queue job
judgmentFindings.detail: POST /api/submissions inserts into esf7_submission_queue whose key is a server-side SERIAL and whose create script (server/create_esf7_submission_queue_table.js) defines no unique (school_id, school_year, client ID). A double click or client retry queues the same submission twice, and each job runs the heavy processing in queue_worker.js.

judgmentFindings.title: Tenant for a submission can come from the request body, with a hardcoded fallback school
judgmentFindings.detail: schoolId is getSchoolIdFromRequest(req) || req.body.schoolId || a literal school number. If the verified lookup returns nothing the body value or a literal id decides which school the data is filed under. The tenant must come only from the verified token.

judgmentFindings.title: One worker job is a very long single transaction
judgmentFindings.detail: The job runs BEGIN at line 621 and COMMIT at line 3020, with deletes and re-inserts across about twenty normalized tables in between, on one checked-out connection. Up to MAX_CONCURRENT_WORKERS = 5 jobs run per process (server/queue_worker.js:516), so during a burst a few jobs can hold connections and row locks for the whole run and starve the web pool if START_LOCAL_WORKER is not false.

judgmentFindings.title: Workload ID is built from COUNT(*) of the whole table
judgmentFindings.detail: POST /api/workloads reads SELECT COUNT(*) FROM esf7_workload_rows and uses count+1 in the new id. Two simultaneous saves can read the same count; the id collides or the save fails. Use a sequence or a client-generated UUID.

judgmentFindings.title: Redis carries only a job pointer; PostgreSQL is already the durable store
judgmentFindings.detail: The payload is committed to esf7_submission_queue first and Redis (XADD with jobId, schoolId, schoolYear) is a best-effort wake-up with a polling fallback. This is already an outbox pattern: an accepted submission survives a Redis outage. The residual risks are the payload size in the queue table, the unbounded body limit, and worker throughput, not Redis durability.

judgmentFindings.title: Client retry backoff has no jitter; draft retry is a fixed 10 s
judgmentFindings.detail: fetchJsonWithRetry retries 502/503/504 at 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s without randomization, and the draft saver retries every 10 s. After an outage all clients retry on the same schedule.

judgmentFindings.title: Request body limit is 50 MB while the queue payload is stored whole
judgmentFindings.detail: express.json({ limit: '50mb' }) lets each request hold up to 50 MB in memory before any validation. A burst of large certified payloads is held in the Node process (1500M restart limit per PM2 app) and then written whole into a JSONB column.
